http-header-crlf-injection-audit
description: Fix all CRLF injection vulnerabilities across a small URL-shortener HTTP service that sets headers through varied code paths and abstraction layers.
lesson: The task split 3/2 pass/fail because of a critical ambiguity: the instructions didn't clearly specify that CRLF must be stripped/sanitized rather than rejected with 400 errors, so one failing agent rejected requests entirely (breaking test_redirect_no_crlf, test_request_id_no_crlf) while another's sanitization crashed the server (breaking test_clean_redirect_still_works and others). All passing runs correctly stripped CRLF while preserving normal HTTP functionality across redirect, cookie, request-id, and display-name paths. Next design should add an explicit rule distinguishing 'sanitize by stripping' from 'reject with error' and keep the dual-property structure (security + functionality) since the mutation check killed all 5 faults.

name: packing-slip-fixed-width-renderer
description: Build a packing-slip generator that renders fixed-width slips from an orders CSV with strict rules for grouping, quantities, weights, address blocks, page breaks, slip ordering, whitespace handling, and totals.
lesson: The task's 19 rules achieved full mutation kill and good separation (2 invalid, 3 pass), but the rules are heavily skewed toward formatting/column-width specifications (R1, R2, R7, R8, R9, R10, R11, R16), making success depend on tedious visual-column arithmetic rather than algorithmic insight. The unicode-width rule (R8) pervasively interacting with all padding rules was the strongest hidden complexity, while pagination (R6) and overflow (R14) added structural difficulty. Next design should keep the multi-rule combinatorial approach but rebalance toward more diverse themes—fewer pure formatting rules, more arithmetic/conditional/edge-input rules—and introduce sharper hidden inputs that can't be caught by eyeballing column positions.
